❗️This is a potentially dangerous situation for the central Phillipines as typhoon Kalmaegi is forecast to make landfall Monday night over the eastern Visayas region as a high-end T4 or low-end T5 storm bringing locally destructive winds and flooding rains❗️ 

*Analasis created at 10:00 am Sunday PST, Nov 2nd* 

Typhoon Hazards for the Central Phillipines: 
• Wind gusts: Locally up to 200km/h or higher
• Rainfall amounts: Locally 400 mm or more 
• Swells 20 to 25 feet over the Eastern Visayas shores, ranging 10 to 15 feet for the surrounding regions 

Regions in the Philippines in the path of Kalmaegi: 
• Eastern Visayas 
• Central Visayas
• Western Visayas 
• Negros Island Region 
• Northern Mindanao • Caraga 

Recommended actions: 
Preparations to protect property for destructive winds should begin today and be completed on Monday. Heavy rains will begin over the Eastern Visayas in 24 hours, and spread inland, prepare for potential evacuation orders. 

Overview and Storm analysis: 

Tropical Storm Kalmaegi has formed in the Phillipine Sea early this morning, and is traveling west towards the Eastern Visayas region. 
The storm is 36 hours from landfall, and over the next 24 hours, is forecast to steadily intensify into a typhoon, with sustained winds of at least 120km/h. 
Most models are triggering a period of RI (Rapid intensification) beginning in 12 to 24 hours and continuing until landfall, with our peak intensity forecast currently increased from 140 to 160km/h at 2:00 this morning, to 170km/h for this update at 10:00 am. 

Note that this number is subject to modification in our next update, especially given the current model uncertainty. 

The ECMWF projections are by far more severe then the rest of the models, suggesting Kalmaegi  explosively intensifying over the next 36 hours and possibly making landfall as a super typhoon with sustained winds of at least 240km/h. 
The ECMWF is a highly reputable model, however the HAFS-A, a mesoscale model proven to be highly accurate during recent super hurricane Melissa, sits on the lower end of the intensity spectrum, and so our forecast currently lies in the middle of the uncertainty. 
ICON is believed as an outlier at this time, projecting Kalmaegi never even reaches typhoon status, though this projection is not being taken account for in our model blend. 

A lot of details should be made clear over the next 12 to 24 hours, so please stay tuned for further forecasts for the Phillipines. 

Once the Kalmaegi exits the Philippines, the storm should enter another favourable environment over the South China Sea, where it’ll stay on its westward track towards Vietnam. 

Our current peak intensity forecast for Kalmaegi over the South China Sea is 215km/h, a low-end T6 typhoon, which is currently expected to slam Vietnam with destructive winds and flooding rains on Nov 7th. 

Please stay tuned for updates! 
#TyphoonKalmaegi #Typhoon #Kalmaegi #Phillipines #Vietnam
